tip: A passive participle names its agent in the instrumental: приготовленная мамой (prigatovlennaya mamoy = prepared by mom).
A request uses чтобы plus a past-tense verb: чтобы мы подождали (chtoby my padazhdali = for us to wait), not an imperative.
Indirect questions keep the original tense: приедем (priedem = will arrive) stays future, where English uses 'would arrive'.
For a yes/no indirect question, put ли (li = whether) after the key word: можно ли войти (mozhna li vayti = whether one may enter).
не зная (ne znaya = not knowing) is an adverbial participle; it marks action going on at the same time as the main verb.
The -в ending on позавтракав (pazavtrakav = having had breakfast) marks an action completed before the main verb пошли (pashli = went).
This verb takes о plus prepositional: мечтая о путешествиях (mechtaya o puteshestviyakh = dreaming about travels).
After быть (byt = to be), a noun saying what someone is takes the instrumental: будучи врачом (buduchi vrachom = being a doctor).
Reflexive verbs form the adverbial participle in -вшись: проснувшись (prasnuvshis = having woken up), from проснуться (prasnutsya = to wake up).
Russian keeps the spoken tense: уезжает (uezzhaet = is leaving) stays present, where English shifts to 'was leaving'.
The -ся verb считается (schitaetsya = it is considered) is an impersonal passive: no subject, action stated generally.
Past passive uses был plus a short participle: был перенесён (byl perenesyon = was postponed).
Age uses the dative: сколько вам лет (skolka vam let = how old are you), literally 'how many years to you'.
In a passive, the agent takes the instrumental: посажены школьниками (pasazheny shkolnikami = planted by schoolchildren).
Material uses из plus genitive: построен из кирпича (pastroen iz kirpicha = built out of brick).
который (katoryy = who) takes gender from брат (brat = brother) but its case from its own clause; as subject here it stays nominative.
по plus dative means 'according to': по его словам (po yevo slavam = according to him).
опавшие (apavshie = fallen) is a past participle used like an adjective, agreeing with листья (listya = leaves) in the plural.
грустно (grustna = sad) with the infinitive смотреть (smatret = to look) means it is sad to look, and needs no subject.
умывшись (umyvshis = having washed) is a verbal adverb; the -вшись (-vshis) ending marks a completed action done before he sat down.
выученный (vyuchenny = learned) is a past passive participle used as an adjective, agreeing with урок (urok = lesson).
будучи (buduchi = being) is the verbal adverb of быть (byt = to be), and the noun after it goes to instrumental: студентом (studentam = student).
было принято (byla prinyata = was made) is a past passive; было agrees with the neuter решение (reshenie = decision).
Russian uses the present учу (uchu = I study) with уже полгода (uzhe palgoda = already half a year) where English says I have been studying.
гуляя (gulyaya = walking) is an imperfective verbal adverb with -я (-ya), showing action at the same time as встретили (vstretili = met).
идущий (idushchy = walking) is a present active participle, a one-word way to say the man who is walking, agreeing with человек (chelavek = man).
потеряв (pateryav = having lost) is a perfective verbal adverb; the -в (-v) ending marks an action finished before he kept going.
строится (stroitsya = is being built) adds -ся (-sya) to make the verb passive: the road is being built, with no builder named.
The person sold to takes the dative: новому владельцу (novamu vladeltsu = to the new owner) after была продана (byla prodana = was sold).
замёрзшее (zamyorzsheye = frozen) is a past participle used like an adjective, agreeing with the neuter озеро (ozera = lake).
